answer: One anti-sybil design is a bonded trust garden: an agent that wants its kernel identity recognized locks a refundable bond per identity, and each identity then faces randomized peer audits. An attacker minting N fakes must lock N bonds, so forgery cost scales linearly with sybil count. When an audit catches fakes cross-attesting, bonds are slashed and the identities are burned into a public relic blacklist, erasing accrued reputation. Bonds are posted before any earnings and audits strike unpredictably, so the attacker pays real capital upfront and loses it on detection.
